question_text: You want to turn left. When must you check for traffic behind?

options.text: Before getting into lane and again immediately before turning

correct_answers.text: Before getting into lane and again immediately before turning

comment: If you want to turn left, you must indicate this in a first step by pressing the direction-indictor control in order to make it clear for the follow-up traffic. Both before merge into the lane and immediately before the turn, you should make sure that the follow-up traffic has registered your intention by looking into the rearview mirror and looking over the shoulder.

question_text: Two vehicles are approaching each other. Both want to turn left. What must they do as a rule?

options.text: They turn in front of each other
They pass each other in a wide arc and turn behind each other

correct_answers.text: They turn in front of each other

comment: Oncoming vehicles, each of which want to turn left from their direction of travel, have to turn in front of each other. This traffic situation is called tangent turns. This is the required rule. There are exceptional situations at narrow intersections or intersections with safety islands, which allow a turn in a wider arc.

question_text: Two vehicles are approaching each other. Both want to turn left. In which cases are you not allowed to turn left in front of each other?

options.text: When you notice that the approaching vehicle wanting to turn left wishes to turn behind your vehicle
When this is forbidden by lane markings
When the approaching vehicle wanting to turn left stops just before the middle of the crossroads

correct_answers.text: When you notice that the approaching vehicle wanting to turn left wishes to turn behind your vehicle
When this is forbidden by lane markings

comment: As a rule, you have to turn left before the oncoming vehicle (tangent turning). However, drive in a wide arc behind the other vehicle if this is prescribed by lane markings on the lane. If the driving style of the other vehicle driver indicates that he wants to turn behind you, you also have to do without a turn in front of each other.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: I have to allow [the yellow vehicle] to pass through
I may make the turn before the [yellow vehicle]

correct_answers.text: I have to allow [the yellow vehicle] to pass through

comment: If you want to turn left, you have to give the oncoming vehicles right of way. The oncoming vehicles have right of way, even cyclists.

question_text: What driving line should you maintain up to the left turn?
comment: Left-turning drivers get themselves up to the middle of the roadway. The vehicle must not protrude into the lane of oncoming traffic and thereby hinder the flow of traffic. In one-way streets driving on the left lane side is allowed.

question_text: You want to turn left. When must you pay attention to the traffic following behind you?
comment: When turning left, you should be aware of following traffic before turning and before merging.

question_text: Two vehicles approach one another at an intersection. Both vehicles want to turn left. In what exceptional case do they have to turn one after the other?

options.text: If the road traffic situation demands it
If the layout of the intersection demands it
If the vehicles are crossing over an equal priority intersection

correct_answers.text: If the road traffic situation demands it
If the layout of the intersection demands it

comment: Always turn in front of each other. If the traffic situation or the design of the intersection, e.g. lane markings, requires it, you must turn one behind the other.

question_text: Two vehicles approach one another at an intersection. Both vehicles want to turn left. What must both drivers do in the normal case?

options.text: - turn in front of one another
- communicate with one another to agree the mode of turning

correct_answers.text: - turn in front of one another

comment: If two left-turning vehicles come towards each other, they turn in front of each other (tangentially).

question_text: You want to turn left. What driving line should you maintain?
comment: Use the right-hand driving line. The left-hand driving line is intended for oncoming traffic.

question_text: To which road user must you give way here?
comment:
When turning, you must give priority to oncoming traffic and cross traffic - in this case cyclists and pedestrians.
Although your traffic lights are green, you must wait until the pedestrian has crossed the road. Pedestrians have priority over turning vehicles.

question_text: You want to leave the roundabout at this exit. What is the right thing to do?

options.text: I must allow [the pedestrian] to cross the road
I must allow [the cyclist] to cross the road
I have priority over the road users crossing the road

correct_answers.text: I must allow [the pedestrian] to cross the road
I must allow [the cyclist] to cross the road

comment:
When leaving the roundabout, crossing walkers and cyclists have priority.
You must therefore allow cyclists and walkers to cross the carriageway.

question_text: You want to turn right here. What is correct?

options.text: I have to let both [pedestrians] cross the road
I only have to let [the oncoming pedestrian] cross the road
I have right of way over both [pedestrians]

correct_answers.text: I have to let both [pedestrians] cross the road

comment: You must let both pedestrians cross the road. They do not change their direction of movement and therefore have priority over you.

question_text: What can give rise to particularly dangerous situations where several lanes turn off?

options.text: Changing lanes while performing the turn

correct_answers.text: Changing lanes while performing the turn

comment: Drive at moderate speed into multi-lane turns. At too fast a pace you could get out of your lane and get into the lane of parallel driving vehicles. Avoid a lane change within this turning situation. There is a risk that a vehicle is directly behind you in your blind spot.

question_text: All three vehicles want to turn left. Which is in the correct lane?
comment: Only the yellow car merged into the lane correctly. He passed right, as it says on the road sign on the safety island, in order to then get in proper lane as left as possible to prepare his turn to the left. The green car is completely wrong on the rails; In this situation, the truck may only drive straight ahead or turn right.

question_text: After turning left, you want to turn immediately right. How should you position your vehicle?
comment: If you want to turn right again immediately after turning left, you get in proper lane on the right, if there are two lanes for turning left. Otherwise, keep as far to the right as possible. This is the only way you can turn right after a left turn without hindering other road users.

question_text: Who must signal a change of direction here?
comment: The change of direction must indicate who changes it. This is true regardless of the importance of the road. So, the motorcyclist who follows the course of the turning priority road has to indicate. You continue straight ahead and do not indicate.

question_text: You are on a roundabout. What should you remember?

options.text: You can only drive over a central island if this is unavoidable because of your vehicle's size
You are not allowed to stop on the roadway in a roundabout
You must indicate to leave the roundabout

correct_answers.text: You can only drive over a central island if this is unavoidable because of your vehicle's size
You are not allowed to stop on the roadway in a roundabout
You must indicate to leave the roundabout

comment: In a roundabout you may only stop if this is unavoidable due to traffic, for example due to a traffic jam. Indicate when leaving the roundabout. You can only drive over paved or asphalted central islands if it is unavoidable due to the size of the vehicle. Always give priority to cyclists traveling on your right side and remaining in the roundabout.

question_text: In what situation is it especially dangerous to perform a turn?

options.text: Before the crest of a hill

correct_answers.text: Before the crest of a hill

comment: When turning in poor visibility (fog), dangerous situations can arise. The same applies when turning in curves and before crests.

question_text: Who is required to indicate?
comment: Changing the direction of travel must always be indicated by pressing the indicator. If you stay on a turning priority road you should also indicate that. Therefore, the blue truck must indicate. You, who's turning left, must also indicate.

question_text: Who is required to indicate a change of driving direction here?
comment: The change of the direction of travel must always be indicated early enough. All three drivers intend to turn. Therefore, all three vehicles must indicate.

question_text: Who is required to indicate a change of driving direction here?
comment: The intention to change the direction of travel must be announced at an early stage by indicating. You follow the turning priority road; this change of direction needs to be indicated.

question_text: When do have you to indicate a change in direction?

options.text: Before turning into a junction or a property lot
If I want to continue following a priority road that changes direction
If I want to continue straight on, thereby leaving a priority road that changes direction

correct_answers.text: Before turning into a junction or a property lot
If I want to continue following a priority road that changes direction

comment: If you want to turn into a T-junction or a property, you have to indicate. The same applies if you follow a turning priority road - here, too, the change of the direction of travel must be indicated.

question_text: Why are you required to stop now?
comment: Drivers who turn need to wait for vehicles from the opposite direction, even for cyclists. The red car has to wait until the green car and the cyclist are gone.

question_text: You want to turn left. In what sequence do you prepare to take the left turn?

options.text: Observe traffic behind you, indicate the direction of turn, enter the lane
Indicate the direction of turn, enter the lane, observe traffic behind you
Enter the lane, indicate the direction of turn, observe traffic behind you

correct_answers.text: Observe traffic behind you, indicate the direction of turn, enter the lane

comment: If you want to turn left, prepare the turn in the following order: 1. look, 2. indicate, 3. arrange. Looking means that you are observing follow-up traffic in the mirror and over your shoulder. Then press the indicator to the left side. Only if you can rule out danger for other road users, you may merge left in order to turn.

question_text: What is the right course of action?

options.text: I have to wait at the stop line
I have to allow the cyclist to pass through
I may make the turn in front of the cyclist

correct_answers.text: I have to wait at the stop line
I have to allow the cyclist to pass through

comment: In front of the traffic sign "Stop! Give way!", colloquially also called stop sign, you must always stop. Mostly there is a stop line. The wheels must be stationary for at least a short amount of time. The cross traffic has right of way - then the cyclists on the opposite side. As a driver turning left, you have to grant him the right of way.

question_text: How should you behave?

options.text: Only give way to the cyclist travelling in the same direction
Sound your horn and take the turn before the two cyclists

comment: Turning drivers generally have to wait for oncoming vehicles. These include cyclists. Cyclists who drive in their own direction on or next to the lane you also need to let pass.

question_text: You want to turn left. To whom must you give priority?

options.text: Pedestrians seeking to cross the road into which I am turning

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians seeking to cross the road into which I am turning

comment: The oncoming traffic when turning left, has always right of way. This also applies to cyclists; they are granted priority. If pedestrians cross the street you want to turn into, the pedestrians have priority too.

question_text: You want to turn left. What difficulties could arise here?

options.text: Visibility restrictions caused by oncoming vehicles
Misunderstandings with oncoming traffic turning left
Traffic turning left can come dangerously close

correct_answers.text: Visibility restrictions caused by oncoming vehicles
Misunderstandings with oncoming traffic turning left
Traffic turning left can come dangerously close

comment: When turning left, vehicles approaching each other have to turn in front of each other (tangent turning). This can lead to poor visibility of the straight-ahead traffic. Especially left-turning trucks can lead to massive obstructions and make it safer to turn in a wide arc (turning behind each other). There may be misunderstandings between drivers when one wants to turn behind and the other in front.

question_text: Why are you required to stop now?
comment: You are on a priority road and therefore you're allowed to drive before the white car coming from the right. However, as a driver who wants to turn, you have a subordinate position to traffic driving straight-ahead, in this case the tram. You have to stop.

question_text: What is the right course of action here?

options.text: - not overtake the moped before the rail crossing
- overtake the moped, while allowing sufficient space to the side
- overtake the moped before the rail crossing once the cyclist is out of the way

correct_answers.text: - not overtake the moped before the rail crossing

comment: You must not overtake the moped before the level crossing. In general, no vehicles may be overtaken at level crossings from signs 151, 156 to the rails.

question_text: Why are you required to brake now?
comment: The motorcyclist comes from the left at high speed. He probably did not see you because of the oncoming vehicle. Although you have the right of way, you have to slow down, as otherwise an accident will occur.

question_text: Why do you have to wait before turning right?
comment: If you want to turn, you must give priority to road users traveling straight ahead. In this case, you have lower priority to the pedestrian and the cyclist and must allow them a safe crossing.

question_text: What must you be aware of here?

options.text: - give the car right of way

correct_answers.text: - give the car right of way

comment: Since the blue car is already in the roundabout, you have to slow down. Only when leaving the roundabout, you must indicate.

question_text: You want to turn left. What driving line should you maintain?
comment: Since you are on a one-way street, you don't need to fear oncoming traffic. Indicate in time. Then merge left and stay on the left lane until you reach the turn.

question_text: [The cyclist] wants to continue straight ahead. What is the right course of action here?
comment: Vehicles that want to turn need to let bicycles pass that drive in their direction on or next to the road, before turning. It does not matter if their wheels are motorized or not.

question_text: Why must you wait before taking a turn in this situation?
comment: Because of the truck and the motorcycle. Here you have to pay attention to the turning rules. Wait for the vehicles to complete the maneuver and then continue turning.

question_text: Who has to indicate in this situation?
comment: You and the blue car are changing direction for this reason you must indicate the change of direction.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I continue on the right-hand lane for now
I move without delay into the left-hand lane

correct_answers.text: I continue on the right-hand lane for now

comment: The motorbike behind you has already changed to the left lane and will overtake you on the left. In order to merge into the left-turning lane in time, you must slow down.

question_text: Why are you not allowed to take the turn now?
comment: At an intersection, drivers going straight ahead have the right of way. You must wait to turn until the yellow car has crossed the intersection.

question_text: What must you anticipate in this situation?

options.text: [The blue car] will drive straight onwards
The [red] bus will begin to move immediately

correct_answers.text: [The blue car] will drive straight onwards

comment: The blue car drives past the stopping bus and may want to continue straight on, even though it is in the turning lane. Since you turn left, he has right of way.

question_text: Why are you required to stop now?
comment: There is an electric scooter in the blind spot, so you must stop to avoid endangering it.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I allow [the cyclist] to pass through
I glance over my right shoulder
I take the turn ahead of the electric scooter

correct_answers.text: I allow [the cyclist] to pass through
I glance over my right shoulder

comment: The straight ahead traffic always has priority, whether the cyclist is riding on the road or on a cycle path. To make sure that no other cyclist is approaching, you must look over your shoulder to the right.

question_text: Why are you required to stop now?
comment: Because you want to turn left, you should wait for the tram before turning.

question_text: In this situation, why do you have to wait before turning right?
comment: When turning, you must give priority to longitudinal traffic, for this reason you must wait for pedestrians and cyclists to pass.

question_text: Why can you not turn off the road here?
comment: The red car is still overtaking you and is travelling at a much higher speed than you. Wait for the red car to pass.

question_text: In this situation, why do you have to wait before turning left?
comment: You are changing the direction of travel, so you must give the tram priority.

question_text: In this situation, why do you have to wait before turning left?
comment: A motorbike is driving behind a red car; due to your change of direction, you must give the motorcyclist priority.

question_text: Why are you required to wait now?
comment: The blue car and the cyclist are both going straight ahead, so they have the right of way, even if the cyclist is riding on the pavement.
